geometry.locator: Letter of Intent for KM3NeT 2.0 (arXiv:1601.07459), Figure 15 caption
geometry.note: 12-vertex geodesic circle approximation, radius 500 m computed on R=6371008.8 m (the destination-point formula) from the centre (16.1000000, 36.2667000); simplification well within the 2000 m accuracy_m of the shape.
geometry.quote: The instrumented volume is 0.48 km3 (R=500 m, z=612 m)

method: A 500 m radius circle centred on the surveyed ARCA site coordinate (geometry:km3net-arca-site-point, the same published '36°16' N 16°06' E'). The radius is the Letter of Intent for KM3NeT 2.0's own figure-15 caption for one ARCA building block: 'The instrumented volume is 0.48 km3 (R=500 m, z=612 m)'. accuracy_m is set to 2000 m, not the far tighter shape itself, because the circle's true centre is only known to the site coordinate's own arc-minute precision (2000 m) -- the derivation may not rest on an anchor coarser than its own stated accuracy, so accuracy_m is raised to match that anchor rather than showing a falsely precise 500 m-accurate circle. ARCA's full design is two such building blocks (230 detection units total, ~1 km3); only one representative block radius is drawn here since the Letter of Intent gives a per-block figure, not a combined two-block footprint.
name: KM3NeT/ARCA building-block footprint (derived circle)
notes: No checks[] row: the circle's radius IS the sourced LoI figure (R=500 m), so a span check against that same number would be tautological (draw exactly R, then check that R measures R), not an independent cross-check -- the same reasoning docs/atlas-worklog/GEOMETRY_cern.md gives for the TI12/TI18 derived points. A genuine independent check would need a second, different official figure for ARCA's footprint (e.g. a horizontal span stated in an unrelated paper); none was fetched this session.

summary.plain: A schematic circle showing the roughly 1 km design width of one KM3NeT/ARCA building block of 115 detection-unit strings, centred on the telescope's published seabed location.
